messages:
Anya (PM): Folks — we need to lock the 'onboarding priority lanes' and the customer commitment terms for catalog onboarding this quarter. Can we decide lane definitions, acceptance criteria, and what triggers a pinned-version SLA?
James (Eng): +1. what are the proposed lanes?
Anya (PM): Thinking 3 lanes: Lane 1 = Enterprise (SLA, dedicated support, pinning allowed), Lane 2 = Strategic SMB (fast onboarding, limited pin exceptions), Lane 3 = Community / self-serve (best-effort).
Michelle (Solutions): That aligns with asks from BigCorp and ScaleInc. They want ability to request a pinned version for 90d and a rollback window.
Dave (CS): Customers expect a guaranteed performance baseline (p90 latency) and evaluation benchmarks. Can we specify exact metrics?
Sasha (ProductOps): Draft acceptance checklist suggestion: ```- perf: p50/p90 token latency within X ms vs baseline
- quality: eval set pass rate >= Y%
- infra: verified quantization compatibility and fallback plan
- security: no PII exfil risks in synthetic prompts```
James (Eng): Perf numbers need to be hardware-dependent. Suggest we make lane-specific thresholds: Lane1 tighter, Lane2 moderate, Lane3 none. Also require a canary rollout for Lane1 with 48h monitoring.
Anya (PM): Good. For pinning: Lane1 gets pinning as contract add-on (auto-renew 90d). Lane2 gets pin exceptions with product sign-off. Lane3 no pins.
Michelle (Solutions): For migrations: customers with pins need a migration runway: 30d notice + optional opt-in early testing environment. And rollback policy: if regressions > threshold, auto-rollback.
Dave (CS): Thresholds: quality regression > 2% absolute on core eval or error rate spike > 5% => rollback. Also include cost delta guardrails (>30% cost increase triggers ops review).
legal-bot: Reminder: any SLA that promises pinned versions must include termination and force-migration clauses. Need legal review for export controls and data residency language.
Sasha (ProductOps): Timeline proposal: finalize lane definitions by EOW, bake acceptance checklist into onboarding flow next sprint, and add contract template for pinning to sales playbook.
Anya (PM): Action items: James to write canary + rollback runbook, Michelle to draft customer comms and opt-in flow, Sasha to update onboarding UI with lane selection, legal-bot to queue contract language. Due: Friday.
James (Eng): I'll mock a canary playbook today. Quick question: do we allow short-term emergency pins (e.g., 7d) outside of contract?
Anya (PM): Yes — emergency pins allowed but require ops approval and audit trail. We'll limit to one emergency pin per 12 months per customer unless escalated.
Michelle (Solutions): Noted. Also propose a 'grace period' for deprecated models: 60d for Lane1, 30d for Lane2, 7d for Lane3.
Dave (CS): Add monitoring hooks: per-customer evaluation diffs and alerts to #incidents if regression crosses thresholds.
Sasha (ProductOps): I'll update the onboarding checklist to include: lane chosen, contract checkbox, canary schedule, rollback SLA, and customer migration contacts.
Anya (PM): Great. If no major objections, we'll ship this doc as RFC and present to sales/legal on Thursday. :thumbsup:
James (Eng): No objections from eng side. Will post runbook draft in this thread.
Michelle (Solutions): Will loop in BigCorp contacts for review.
legal-bot: Filed: LEG-2026-145 — legal review requested.
Anya (PM): Thanks everyone — short sync on Thursday 10am to sign off.
